talking_points.headline: HKMA initiatives raise planning questions for bank technology and governance
talking_points.context_html: The HKMA has issued a post-quantum toolkit and opened discussion on governance for agentic AI, alongside tokenized-settlement work. Banks may need to coordinate cryptographic inventory and migration planning with separate accountability and control design for AI agents. The article describes a toolkit and proposals, not final supervisory requirements or a fixed migration timetable.

talking_points.headline: Family-office survey points to continuity and cyber-readiness gaps
talking_points.context_html: The DBS-commissioned survey reports limited tested continuity planning and unresolved cybersecurity and data-privacy risks among respondents. In wealth delivery, these gaps may make implementation capacity and family governance as important as identifying a succession or technology need; advisers could ask who owns continuity arrangements and how they are tested. The figures come from a survey of more than 200 family offices and should not be generalized to all clients.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Hong Kong Prepares Banks for Quantum Era and AI Agents
Regulatory & Markets.summary: The HKMA announced initiatives on post-quantum cryptography, agentic AI, tokenized settlement and cross-border payments at Hong Kong FinTech Week. Its PQC Toolkit is intended to help banks plan cryptographic migration, while Project SAGE includes a discussion paper on supervisory requirements for agentic AI. These initiatives make migration planning, governance and accountability relevant execution topics for banks in Hong Kong; the reported proposals and trials are not equivalent to final requirements or broad operational adoption.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Chief Executive Welcomes Global Leaders to Hong Kong FinTech Week x StartmeupHK 2026
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee's FinTech Week speech described government plans for innovation and technology development, and cited growth in fintech firms, wealth inflows and company investment. The speech frames Hong Kong's policy direction and ambitions; it does not announce a specific banking change or establish that projected development will occur as described.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: DBS report finds family offices underprepared for succession and risk events - Private Banker International
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: A DBS-commissioned survey of more than 200 family offices found gaps in succession, continuity planning, risk management and AI readiness. It reports that 43% said the next generation does not participate in wealth planning, more than 85% lack a formal, regularly tested business-continuity plan, and 38% have not addressed cybersecurity and data privacy risk. The findings point to potential client needs around governance, continuity and technology adoption, but are survey results rather than a measure of all family offices.

AI & Technology.title: AI agents could render traditional payment authentication obsolete, warns Dr Ruth Wandhöfer
AI & Technology.summary: At an Open Banking Expo keynote, Ruth Wandhöfer argued that AI agents may change payment authentication, fraud controls and customer relationships, and called for machine-readable consent, agent identity checks and auditable decision records. These are expert views about a possible direction, not established adoption or settled requirements. For change execution, a practical question is how delegated authority and human oversight would be evidenced across an agent-led transaction; the article does not set out a bank implementation or regulatory decision.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Canadian banks blocking AI agents amid security concerns
Competitor Intelligence.summary: The article reports that RBC, TD, CIBC and Scotiabank block or limit third-party AI agents from accessing online banking, and attributes the moves partly to security concerns and reports of unauthorized activity at some US banks. This is another account of Canadian banks' access restrictions; it adds the reported US unauthorized-activity rationale, but does not establish the scale or circumstances of those incidents or a common industry standard.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Citi hires from HSBC for newly created global trade role Citi hires from HSBC for newly created global trade role
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Citi appointed Sibel Sirmagul to a newly created global trade business head role, effective 4 January 2027; she joins from HSBC, where she most recently led global network banking propositions. The role covers product strategy, delivery and end-to-end P&L, according to Citi. This is a competitor leadership and trade-delivery change, but the article does not describe specific plans or outcomes.

Competitor Intelligence.title: DBS Bank’s Han Kwee Juan: From Singapore-Centric to Global Powerhouse - Global Finance Magazine
Competitor Intelligence.summary: DBS Group Head of Institutional Banking Han Kwee Juan said clients are adopting local-for-local and region-for-region supply-chain strategies, and described the bank's use of agentic AI, including a credit-memo solution rolled out to all relationship managers. He also discussed DBS's readiness to interact with clients' AI agents. These are competitor-reported approaches that may inform questions about workflow redesign and human review; the interview does not provide outcome measures or independent validation.

Competitor Intelligence.title: GXS Bank Names Harikrishnan Raguraman as Chief Technology Officer
Competitor Intelligence.summary: GXS Bank appointed Harikrishnan Raguraman as CTO after several senior technology roles at the digital bank. Earlier descriptions of his remit included enterprise technology, generative AI, data and technology strategy. The appointment is a technology-leadership change at an APAC digital bank; the article does not specify a new programme or expected outcomes.
